style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #d5a6bd;\"\u003EWhat is the\u0026nbsp;Epidemiology of the IBD.\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe North American incidence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) ranges from 2.2 to 19.2 cases per 100,000 person-years for ulcerative colitis and 3.1 to 20.2 cases per 200,000 person-years for CD. Prevalence in the United States of adult ulcerative colitis was 238 per 100,000 population and 201 per 100,000 population from data in a large study based on insurance claims.\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #ffd966;\"\u003E \u003Cspan\u003EIBD is much more prevalent in North America and Europe than in Asia or Africa. \u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003EAlthough most IBD occurs in people aged 15 to 30 years, up to 25% of patients will develop IBD by adolescence.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;There appears to be a bimodal distribution with a second peak of 10% to 15% developing IBD after age 60.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECrohn disease is slightly more common in females compared to males, but ulcerative colitis appears to be equally present in both genders. IBD is generally a disorder in developed countries and colder climates.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK470312\/#:~:text=The%20first%20step%20in%20pharmacologic,the%20dose%20can%20be%20tapered\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK470312\/#:~:text=The%20first%20step%20in%20pharmacologic,the%20dose%20can%20be%20tapered\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #d5a6bd; font-size: large;\"\u003E2. Hygiene Hypothesis And Inflammatory Bowel Disease .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAccording to the hygiene hypothesis, individuals raised in a sanitary environment have a higher risk of developing inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). However, results have been inconsistent. We conducted this systematic review of factors related to environmental hygiene and risk of IBD, Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4992453\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4992453\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #d5a6bd;\"\u003EWhat Could Be The Differential Diagnosis With A Patient With Above Symptoms ?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIrritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS):\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel habits.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgSLlcAFdr7334BaWnYjOvulbod59EPdb82FsFQuF4F91xbFzRx8N0p4yOb2tA94LPacEzthkfW-pHxb9fSDoruHNC8astOIht613TnPbLzUDPA_p1cq7A2P9wnLf9Gh2g0a8qGoV7XzXLhzE4eMhZ0_Xr0nG7ExdPJjzIAZXXM3BypqP9T4w8QvBzA5tuM\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EConditions like Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis can cause chronic inflammation in the digestive tract.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E4. \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #d5a6bd;\"\u003EHow can Radiologic Imaging Help in the Diagnosis of CROHN'S Disease.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEglQ9VFdd1o8PJcG80s9ixNaqbS9zunfRhVR7dQ79_yILRnpiht3z1dlUOYLJ4ceww5p3G--eU-_K1ffb4i5jmtfplN1LsylHAUlLVL3yU7tgdSrp2QlpB5agkbUKm6q6SwoX3U07ffj1kjT9wJSG4ivDIsE9LqTtc5RwQjU19xuT4Dmm8h2kD6wXDnq-BF\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #a2c4c9;\"\u003EShowing Thickening of the Wall of Terminal Ileum in our Patient.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERadiologic imaging plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and management of Crohn’s disease (CD). With cross-sectional imaging techniques in particular, the bowel lumen, wall, and extraintestinal manifestations of the disease can be visualized efficiently and noninvasively. Computed tomography enterography (CTE) and magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) are the new gold standards of imaging inflammatory bowel disease, replacing the small-bowel follow-through as the first-line imaging test of choice.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s40134-013-0026-8\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s40134-013-0026-8\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5. \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #ead1dc;\"\u003EWhat is The Treatment ?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe first step in pharmacologic therapy for IBD is \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #04ff00;\"\u003Eaminosalicylates\u003C\/span\u003E. If the patient does not respond to an appropriate dose of aminosalicylates, the second step is the addition of corticosteroids, which tend to result in a significant decrease in inflammation. Once the response is seen, the dose can be tapered.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.mayoclinic.org\/diseases-conditions\/inflammatory-bowel-disease\/diagnosis-treatment\/drc-20353320\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.mayoclinic.org\/diseases-conditions\/inflammatory-bowel-disease\/diagnosis-treatment\/drc-20353320\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #ead1dc; font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E6. Rationale Behind Using Rifaximin in IBD.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERifaximin is a non-systemic antibiotic, since it is essentially non-absorbable from the gut. It has particular indications for traveller’s diarrhoea. \u003Cspan style=\"background-color: #b6d7a8;\"\u003EThere has been interest in recent years in the potential roles of rifaximin in CD.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s10620-010-1140-6\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s10620-010-1140-6\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E[21\/12, 8:04 am] Rakesh Biswas Sir GM HOD:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWell done.
